newsitem.title: NORWAY: Loadings, output returning to normal Statoil field.
newsitem.headline: Loadings, output returning to normal Statoil field.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Monday all operations at the North Sea Statfjord and Gullfaks oilfields were returning to normal following production and loading disruptions due to bad weather.
"There is loading at all platforms and we are resuming normal production as we load," Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said.
"You can start bringing up (crude) production as soon as you hook up the tankers," she said.

Statfjord pumps about 380,000 barrels per day (bpd) and process oil from the Statfjord East and North satellites and the nearby Snorre development, which add roughly 370,000 bpd to the Statfjord stream.
Gullfaks produces around 475,000 bpd and handles around 115,000 bpd from the Tordis and Vigdis fields.
Bjoern Schibevaag, a spokesman for Saga Petroleum ASA, operator of Snorre, Vigdis and Tordis, said Snorre and Vigdis should resume throughput by around midnignt.
"If Gullfaks C is in production, so is Tordis," he said.

Production at the installations was reduced at the weekend after high winds and swell prevented shuttle tankers from mooring at the offshore loadings buoys on Friday and oil storage capacity neared brimming.
